title: Descent and derived naturality of the virtual-rank-one cofactor map
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $L\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category] be locally represented in degrees $-1,0$ by complexes $E_i=[P_i\xrightarrow{u_i}Q_i]$ of finite locally free modules [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module], of ranks $c_i,c_i+1$, with specified derived isomorphisms $\lambda_i:E_i\simeq L|_{U_i}$ on an open cover $(U_i)$. The nonnegative integer $c_i$ may vary between models. Let $D=\det L$ and $d_i:D(E_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}D|_{U_i}$ be the determinant comparisons of [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant], normalized by the kernel-first convention of [lem-sfb-two-term-cofactor-naturality], with $D(E_i)=(\bigwedge^{c_i}P_i)^\vee\otimes\bigwedge^{c_i+1}Q_i$, $(-)^\vee=\mathcal Hom(-,\mathcal O_X)$, and exterior powers as in [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power]. Let $w_i:\operatorname{coker}u_i\to D(E_i)$ be the locally defined wedge map
$$\bar v\longmapsto(p_1\wedge\cdots\wedge p_{c_i})^\vee\otimes(u_i(p_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge u_i(p_{c_i})\wedge v),$$
for a local basis $(p_a)$ and any lift $v$. On every overlap, with $t_{ij}=d_j^{-1}d_i$, these maps satisfy
$$t_{ij}w_i=w_jH^0(\lambda_j^{-1}\lambda_i).$$
Consequently there is a unique $\mathcal O_X$-linear morphism $w_L:H^0(L)\to D$ whose expression through every specified model is $d_iw_i$. It has this expression in every further two-term finite locally free model of the same rank difference, even one absent from the given cover. These assertions hold on arbitrary overlaps without separatedness of $X$ or affineness of intersections. For every derived isomorphism $b:L\simeq M$ between two such objects, $\det(b)w_L=w_MH^0(b)$. The construction commutes with restriction to open subschemes, refinements, and transport through isomorphisms of schemes, using the canonical cohomology and determinant comparisons. No cotangent origin, smoothness, flatness or Noetherian hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 0E9Y (lemma-determinant), wedge map; more-algebra.tex Tag 0FJM (lemma-determinant-two-term-complexes), intrinsic good-diagram comparison. Agent-formulated sheaf descent of the cofactor naturality statement. Extracts old proof step 4 and the comparison/restriction argument of step 7.

proof.text: Work first on an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset U_i$ on which $P_i,Q_i$ are free; such opens cover $U_i$ by finite local freeness. The affine tilde adjunction identifies the differential with an $A$-linear map $A^{c_i}\to A^{c_i+1}$ and its sheaf cokernel with the associated sheaf of the module cokernel, since tilde preserves cokernels. Apply [lem-sfb-cofactor-local-descent]. It gives the linear cofactor map, independent of basis and lift, and its compatibility with all further localizations. On a free chart the sheaf exterior power is identified with the associated module exterior power by sending a basis wedge to that same wedge; the dual basis and tensor factors give the corresponding identification of $D(E_i)$. These identifications respect restriction by the definition of sheaf exterior powers and the localization comparisons of the cited cofactor lemma. Let $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $V'=\operatorname{Spec}A'$ be two such charts. By [lem-sc-affine-inter-principal-both] every point of $V\cap V'$ lies in an open $W=D_V(f)=D_{V'}(g)$ that is principal in both charts, so $\mathcal O(W)=A_f=A'_g$ is a localization of each ring. On $W$ both chart maps are the scalar extensions of the two module cofactor maps to this common localization; by [lem-sfb-cofactor-local-descent], applied over $A$ and over $A'$, each is given there by the wedge formula for any basis of $P_i|_W$, and this formula does not depend on the basis, so the two maps agree on $W$. Such opens $W$ cover $V\cap V'$. Sheaf-morphism uniqueness then gives equality on the intersection, and sheaf-morphism gluing gives $w_i:\operatorname{coker}u_i\to D(E_i)$ on all of $U_i$. No assertion that an intersection of affine opens is affine is used.

source.place: Tag 0E9Y (lemma-determinant), wedge formula; localization and well-definedness supplied by the cited cofactor lemma; sites-modules.tex Tag 03EM (lemma-internal-hom), sites.tex Tag 04TQ (lemma-glue-maps). proof.text: On an overlap $W=U_i\cap U_j$, choose affine opens $V\subset W$ trivializing all four terms of $E_i,E_j$. Restriction is exact, so $H^0(E_i)|_V=\operatorname{coker}(u_i|_V)$ and likewise for $j$; it also takes the derived isomorphism $a=\lambda_j^{-1}\lambda_i$ to a derived isomorphism on $V$. The termwise-tilde equivalence of [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] is fully faithful into the full subcategory $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_V)$, hence represents this restricted isomorphism by an isomorphism of the two corresponding module complexes in $D(A)$. The normalization in the statement and determinant restriction compatibility identify its determinant map with $t_{ij}|_V$. Apply [lem-sfb-two-term-cofactor-naturality] over $A$: it gives $t_{ij}w_i=w_jH^0(a)$ on $V$. The cohomology identification here is the one induced by termwise tilde and its preservation of cokernels; the maps $w_i,w_j$ are those of step 1 by their formula. Equality holds on all of $W$ by uniqueness for sheaf morphisms on a cover. The algebraic input allows $c_i\ne c_j$, so no equality of the negative ranks has been assumed.

source.place: Tag 0FJM (lemma-determinant-two-term-complexes), derived comparison; perfect.tex Tag 06Z0 (lemma-affine-compare-bounded), affine equivalence; cohomology.tex Tag 08BS, open restriction.

proof.text: Put $h_i=H^0(\lambda_i)$ and $\phi_i=d_iw_i h_i^{-1}:H^0(L)|_{U_i}\to D|_{U_i}$. On $U_i\cap U_j$, step 2 and $H^0(\lambda_j^{-1}\lambda_i)=h_j^{-1}h_i$ give $d_iw_i=d_jw_jh_j^{-1}h_i$, hence $\phi_i=\phi_j$. Apply [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing] on the Zariski site with $F=H^0(L)$ and $G=D$. The fibre products in that lemma are intersections of opens, which exist without separatedness. It gives a unique $\mathcal O_X$-linear $w_L$ restricting to $\phi_i$. In particular $w_Lh_i=d_iw_i$, which is the stipulated expression in each model. If the cover is empty, $X$ is empty and the same sheaf gluing statement gives the unique morphism.

source.place: Tag 03EM (lemma-internal-hom), with sites.tex Tag 04TQ (lemma-glue-maps); algebraic substitution of step 2.

proof.text:
Let $E\simeq L|_T$ be any additional two-term model. Apply the comparison argument of step 2 on each $T\cap U_i$ to this model and $E_i$. It says that the transported map from $E$ equals $w_L|_T$ locally, hence everywhere by sheaf-morphism uniqueness. Thus enlarging or refining the cover gives the same map. Next let $b:L\simeq M$. On a common refinement choose a model $E$ of $L$ and a model $F$ of $M$, with model isomorphisms $\lambda,\mu$. Apply step 2's affine argument to $a=\mu^{-1}b\lambda$. Its cofactor identity, multiplied by the model comparisons and using determinant functoriality, reads
$$\det(b)\,d_Ew_E=d_Fw_F H^0(\mu)^{-1}H^0(b)H^0(\lambda).$$
Use the model formulas for $w_L,w_M$ and cancel the invertible $H^0(\lambda)$ to get $\det(b)w_L=w_MH^0(b)$ locally. Uniqueness for sheaf morphisms gives the equality on $X$.

source.place: Tag 0FJM, functorial determinant comparisons; perfect.tex Tags 0FJX and 0FJY; sites-modules.tex Tag 03EM. Reapplication and cancellation of the comparison proved in step 2.

proof.text:
For an open subscheme $T\subset X$, restrict the specified models and their maps. Exactness of restriction identifies the restricted cokernels with $H^0(L|_T)$. Determinant restriction compatibility identifies their targets with $\det(L|_T)$. Their wedge formulas restrict term by term, so uniqueness from step 3 identifies the restricted $w_L$ with the construction on $T$. Finally let $s:X'\xrightarrow{\sim}X$ be a scheme isomorphism. Pull a free chart and its model back along $s$. On affine charts this is a ring isomorphism $A\to B$; scalar extension is therefore an exact equivalence, and identifies the module cokernels and their cohomology maps. By [lem-trf-projective-exterior-scalar-comparisons] the exterior and dual comparisons send the basis wedge and its dual to the pulled-back basis wedge and dual. Thus the scalar extension of $w(\bar v)$ is exactly
$$(p'_1\wedge\cdots\wedge p'_c)^\vee\otimes\bigl(u'(p'_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge u'(p'_c)\wedge v'\bigr).$$
The determinant pullback comparison is the one in [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant]. The local formulas therefore coincide, and sheaf-morphism uniqueness gives the asserted transport compatibility globally. This argument uses only a ring isomorphism for transport and exact open restriction; no additional geometric hypotheses enter.
